speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Hey. Guess what time I got up today. Six thirty. A.M.

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: Wait— six thirty? You? The guy who goes to bed at seven... in the morning?

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Hey, that was one time. [chuckle] But yeah, I'm really trying to adjust my sleep schedule. And honestly? Waking up early makes me feel like my life is just... full of possibilities.

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: No, I get that. It's a great feeling. Okay so— what else have you been thinking about?

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Food, actually. Like, a lot. I want to eat low-calorie meals, but still make them delicious, you know?

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: Okay, so give me an example. What's a meal you like?

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Alright, so— brown rice, chicken, veggies... and a little sesame sauce on top.

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: Ooh, that's a solid combo. Because brown rice is a whole grain, chicken breast is low in fat, high in protein... that's a great base, right there.

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Right? And don't forget the mushrooms. Dietary fiber, baby.

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: [chuckle] Exactly. And if you throw in broccoli and carrots— low in calories, high in fiber and vitamins. You're basically set.

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Okay, but what about the sesame sauce, though? Is that actually healthy? Be honest.

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: Well... it has some healthy fats, but it's also really calorie-dense.

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: Just a little. A little sesame sauce for flavor, since it's so high in calories.

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Got it, got it. So basically— if I want food that's low calorie but still tasty, I just use spices.

speaker: B
name: Mia
text: Yes. Spices, herbs, vinegar, lemon juice... small amounts of strong sauces. That's the whole trick.

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Okay, so I can say: I use spices, and just a little sauce, to add flavor without too many calories.

speaker: A
name: Alex
text: Ha! Nice. That's what I want to practice saying.
